# Models are generated by Blender scripts and share one palette material

Every model is built by a Python script under `art/blender/` and exported to FBX; the script, not a `.blend` file, is the source of truth. All models are colored by UV-mapping faces onto cells of one palette texture (an 8×8 grid of colors, grown as needed), so the whole game renders with a single material (`Art/Shared/M_Palette.mat`).

## Considered Options

- Hand-modelled `.blend` files: binary, unreviewable in a diff, and needing Blender skills the project does not have. Scripts are text, reviewable, and an agent can iterate on them through MCP for Blender.
- Asset packs or AI-generated models as the main source: inconsistent styles and polycounts; they stay an option for one-off models that are then normalized to the palette and the rules in ADR-0008.
- One material per color: more draw calls on mobile, and colors drift between models.

## Consequences

Generated FBX and PNG are committed (Git LFS) so the project opens without Blender. Their content changes only through the scripts, so a hand edit is lost on the next build. Per-Participant colors need a palette swap or a material property block, not new materials.

## Amendment: third-party models through the same pipeline

Ready-made CC0/CC-BY models are a regular source, not only for one-offs: the farm buildings, fence, well, cauldron and Loot props come from poly.pizza. The downloaded file stays untouched in `art/sources/<author>/` and is credited in `art/CREDITS.md`; its model script loads it with `plow_art/imported.py`, which repaints every face to a palette cell, joins the parts, and scales it to a footprint size. So the script is still the source of truth and the single material holds. A source that cannot be mapped to opaque palette colors (alpha-cut foliage, baked lighting) is replaced by a generated model, as the pine and the woodpile were, or recorded here as an exception.
